high.title: Goodbye, Foreigners? Find Out What Made May Register Foreign 'Flight' from B3 and If It's Time to Follow the Herd
high.summary: Critical capital flow reversal for BRL and Brazilian equities. After massive foreign inflows in early 2026 (January alone saw R$26.5 billion, matching all of 2025), May marked the first net foreign capital withdrawal from B3 at -R$13.8 billion through May 26th. This dramatic reversal stems from Middle East geopolitical tensions affecting global inflation expectations and altering interest rate trajectories worldwide, combined with deteriorating domestic conditions. The shift from R$26.5bn inflows in January to R$13.8bn outflows in May signals a major sentiment change that will pressure BRL/USD and Brazilian asset prices. For FX traders, this represents a fundamental shift in the carry trade dynamics that had been supporting BRL strength. Bond investors should expect increased volatility as foreign demand for Brazilian fixed income weakens. Watch for continued outflows if geopolitical tensions persist and domestic fundamentals don't improve.

high.title: 'Sell in May': May is Ibovespa's Worst Month in 3 Years, But Is It Time to 'Go Away'?
high.summary: Ibovespa suffered its worst monthly performance since 2023, falling approximately 6% in May 2026, validating the "sell in May and go away" strategy. The decline was driven by persistent inflation pressures, political noise, and adverse external conditions including Middle East tensions affecting global risk appetite. This represents the largest monthly drop in three years and creates a critical test for Brazil investment thesis. The selloff was broad-based, affecting multiple sectors and reflecting a combination of domestic policy uncertainty and global risk-off sentiment. For equity investors, this suggests potential further downside if the identified headwinds persist into June. The magnitude of the decline indicates institutional selling pressure that could continue absent positive catalysts. FX implications are negative for BRL as equity outflows typically translate to currency weakness.

high.title: Ibovespa Opens Slightly Higher Despite 25% US Tariffs; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (2)
high.summary: Markets showing resilience despite significant trade policy headwinds. Ibovespa opened up 0.51% at 173,069.70 points while USD/BRL declined to 5.0169 (-0.12%), both moves contradicting the negative implications of new US trade actions. The US Trade Representative recommended implementing 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, citing unfair practices against US companies. The proposal requires public consultation before President Trump can implement it across various sectors. Market's initial sanguine reaction suggests either: 1) expectation that tariffs won't be fully implemented, 2) belief that Brazil can negotiate alternatives, or 3) oversold conditions creating buying opportunities. For traders, this represents a critical inflection point - if tariffs are implemented, expect significant pressure on BRL and export-dependent sectors. The DXY weakness (-0.12% to 99.083) is providing temporary BRL support, but trade war escalation would override this dynamic.

medium.title: Vale (VALE3) Falls More Than 2% This Monday (1st)
medium.summary: Vale shares dropped 2.63% to R$80.64, leading Ibovespa declines amid weak metal commodities and increased global risk aversion. Mining sector broadly pressured with CSN falling 7.45% and iron ore prices declining in Dalian (-0.19%) and Singapore (-0.80%). The selloff reflects both foreign capital outflows from Brazilian equities and geopolitical concerns as Iran suspended negotiations, affecting commodity demand expectations.

medium.title: How Does the Middle East War Affect Prio (PRIO3) and Petrobras (PETR3;PETR4)? Stocks Lead Ibovespa This Monday (1st)
medium.summary: Oil stocks leading Ibovespa gains as geopolitical tensions drive crude prices higher. Prio advanced 3.13%, PETR3 up 3.06%, and PETR4 gained 1.93% following renewed US-Iran military actions. Brent futures jumped 7.11% to $97.57/barrel while WTI surged 8.36% to $94.61/barrel. The energy sector benefits from risk premium pricing as Middle East tensions escalate, providing relative outperformance versus broader market weakness.

medium.title: Exchange Nubank (ROXO34) for Itaú (ITUB4): 10 Stocks to Invest in June and Beat Ibovespa, According to BTG
medium.summary: BTG Pactual adjusted its recommended equity portfolio for June, swapping Nubank for Itaú (15% weight) due to preference for institutions better positioned for restrictive credit environment. The move toward more defensive, higher-quality names reflects challenging conditions for Brazilian assets. BTG also replaced Allos with Equatorial, increasing exposure to utilities and infrastructure sectors.

medium.title: Dollar Maintains Global Leadership Despite US Turbulence; Euro Doesn't Take Off
medium.summary: Euro's global role remained virtually unchanged last year despite erratic US economic policy, with 20% market share across broad indicators. ECB President Lagarde's expectations for euro as viable dollar alternative haven't materialized, as investors moved to gold and smaller reserve currencies instead. This maintains dollar dominance in global reserves, supporting USD strength including against BRL.
